cases.sentence: У портьеры, прислонившись к притолоке, стоял, заложив ногу за ногу, ___ маленького роста и несимпатичной наружности.
cases.translation: By the curtain, leaning against the doorframe with his legs crossed, stood a man of small stature and unpleasant appearance.
cases.explain: «Человек стоял» — the man is the subject of the verb стоял, so he stands in the Nominative.

cases.translation: A person without a document is strictly forbidden to exist.
cases.explain: The preposition «без» (without) governs the Genitive case, so документ becomes документа.

cases.sentence: Филипп Филиппович к ___ подошел вплотную и шепнул удушливо.
cases.translation: Filipp Filippovich walked right up to the old woman and hissed at her chokingly.
cases.explain: The preposition «к» (up to/toward) governs the Dative case, so старуха becomes старухе.

cases.translation: Filipp Filippovich spoke into the receiver: yes.
cases.explain: The preposition «в» expressing direction (speaking into) governs the Accusative, so трубка becomes трубку.

cases.sentence: На шее у человека был повязан ядовито – небесного цвета галстук с фальшивой рубиновой ___.
cases.translation: Around the man's neck was tied a poisonous sky-blue necktie with a fake ruby pin.
cases.explain: The preposition «с» meaning "with/having" governs the Instrumental case, so булавка becomes булавкой.

cases.sentence: Нет ли у вас в ___ свободной комнаты?
cases.translation: Don't you have a free room in the building?
cases.explain: The preposition «в» expressing location governs the Prepositional case, so дом becomes доме.

reading.ru: Семечки есть в квартире, запрещаю.
reading.question: What does the sign on the door to the reception room, written by Filipp Filippovich, forbid?
options: Eating sunflower seeds in the apartment
reading.correct: Eating sunflower seeds in the apartment
reading.explain: The professor's note reads: 'Eating sunflower seeds in the apartment, I forbid it.'

reading.ru: Филипп Филиппович, склонившись над столом, погрузился в развернутый громадный лист газеты.
reading.question: What is Filipp Filippovich doing at the start of the dinner scene?
options: Bent over the table, absorbed in reading a huge unfolded newspaper
reading.correct: Bent over the table, absorbed in reading a huge unfolded newspaper
reading.explain: He is bent over the table, absorbed in a huge unfolded sheet of newspaper, his face twisted by what he reads.

reading.ru: У портьеры, прислонившись к притолоке, стоял, заложив ногу на ногу, человек маленького роста и несимпатичной наружности.
reading.question: How is the man standing by the curtain (Sharikov) described physically?
reading.correct: Short and unpleasant-looking
reading.explain: The man leaning at the doorway with crossed legs is described as short in stature and unpleasant in appearance.

reading.ru: На шее у человека был повязан ядовито-небесного цвета галстук с фальшивой рубиновой булавкой.
reading.question: What is notable about the necktie the man is wearing?
options: It is a poisonous sky-blue color with a fake ruby pin
It is plain black and simple
It was a gift from the professor
reading.correct: It is a poisonous sky-blue color with a fake ruby pin
reading.explain: Around his neck is tied a garishly bright sky-blue necktie with a fake ruby pin, which dazzles Filipp Filippovich's eyes.

reading.ru: «Я, кажется, два раза уже просил не спать на палатях в кухне, тем более днем».
reading.question: What has Filipp Filippovich already asked Sharikov twice not to do?
options: Sleep on the shelf above the stove in the kitchen, especially during the day
Wear his boots inside the house
reading.correct: Sleep on the shelf above the stove in the kitchen, especially during the day
reading.explain: Filipp Filippovich says he has already asked twice that Sharikov not sleep on the kitchen sleeping-shelf, especially in the daytime.

reading.ru: «Шикарный галстук Дарья Петровна подарила».
reading.question: According to Sharikov, who gave him the flashy necktie?
reading.correct: Darya Petrovna
reading.explain: Sharikov proudly claims that Darya Petrovna gave him the 'stylish' necktie as a gift.

reading.ru: Разве я просил мне операцию делать?
reading.question: What argument does Sharikov make to justify his rude behavior?
options: That he never asked to have the operation performed on him
That he was forced to move into the apartment
That he was promised money for good behavior
That the professor owes him an apology for the collar
reading.correct: That he never asked to have the operation performed on him
reading.explain: Sharikov protests that he never asked for the operation to be done to him, so he feels he owes no gratitude.

reading.ru: Документ, Филипп Филиппович, мне надо».
reading.question: What does Sharikov say he urgently needs from the professor?
reading.correct: Identity documents/papers
reading.explain: Sharikov states plainly that what he needs is a document (identity papers).

reading.ru: Они говорят, где же это видано, чтобы человек проживал непрописанный в Москве.
reading.question: What argument does Sharikov attribute to the house committee about living in Moscow?
options: That it is unheard of for a person to live in Moscow without being registered
That only Muscovites by birth may live there
That everyone must pay extra taxes
That pets are not allowed in the building
reading.correct: That it is unheard of for a person to live in Moscow without being registered
reading.explain: Sharikov quotes the house committee's view that it is unheard of for someone to live in Moscow unregistered.

reading.ru: Имя я себе совершенно спокойно могу избрать.
reading.question: How does Sharikov respond when told he has neither a first name nor a surname?
options: He says he can calmly choose a name for himself
He becomes furious and refuses to discuss it
He asks the professor to choose for him
He insists he already has a name
reading.correct: He says he can calmly choose a name for himself
reading.explain: Sharikov calmly states that he can perfectly well choose his own first name.

reading.ru: Фамилию я согласен наследственную принять.
reading.question: What does Sharikov say about choosing his surname?
options: That he agrees to take a hereditary surname (from the house calendar)
That he refuses to have any surname at all
That he wants Filipp Filippovich's own surname
That the committee must decide it for him
reading.correct: That he agrees to take a hereditary surname (from the house calendar)
reading.explain: Sharikov agrees to accept a 'hereditary' surname, which turns out to be Sharikov, taken from the calendar's saint's-day listing.

reading.ru: Предъявитель всего действительно Шариков Полиграф Полиграфович».
reading.question: What official-sounding phrase does Shvonder want written into the certificate?
options: That the bearer is indeed Sharikov Poligraf Poligrafovich
That the bearer is a wanted criminal
That the bearer is a foreign citizen
That the bearer is Professor Preobrazhensky's son
reading.correct: That the bearer is indeed Sharikov Poligraf Poligrafovich
reading.explain: Shvonder dictates that the certificate should state the bearer is indeed Sharikov, Poligraf Poligrafovich.

reading.ru: Документ – самая важная вещь на свете».
reading.question: What does Shvonder declare about documents?
options: That a document is the most important thing in the world
That the professor should not need one himself
reading.correct: That a document is the most important thing in the world
reading.explain: Shvonder insists a document is the single most important thing in existence, defending Sharikov's right to discuss his own papers.

reading.ru: Предъявитель всего человек, полученный при лабораторном опыте путем операции на головном мозгу, нуждается в документах.
reading.question: How does Filipp Filippovich phrase the certificate he angrily writes out?
options: That the bearer is a being produced by a laboratory experiment via a brain operation, and needs documents
That the bearer is an ordinary citizen with no special history
That the bearer should be arrested immediately
That the bearer is his adopted son
reading.correct: That the bearer is a being produced by a laboratory experiment via a brain operation, and needs documents
reading.explain: Furious, Filipp Filippovich writes that the bearer is a being obtained through a laboratory experiment by an operation on the brain, and requires documents.

reading.ru: «Меня вишь, как отделали?» – и он показал на голову.
reading.question: What does Sharikov point to as proof of his suffering?
options: The scar on his head from the operation
reading.correct: The scar on his head from the operation
reading.explain: Sharikov complains about how he was 'fixed up,' pointing to his head, where a fresh operation scar runs across his forehead.

reading.ru: «Нет ли у вас в доме свободной комнаты?
reading.question: What does Filipp Filippovich ask Shvonder, hoping to solve his problem with Sharikov?
options: Whether there is a free room in the building he could buy
Whether Shvonder can find Sharikov a job
Whether the committee can take Sharikov away entirely
Whether Shvonder can lend him money
reading.correct: Whether there is a free room in the building he could buy
reading.explain: Struck by a sudden thought, Filipp Filippovich asks whether there is a free room in the building that he could purchase, presumably to house Sharikov separately.

reading.ru: «Боже мой, еще что-то!» – закричал Филипп Филиппович, бросаясь к дверям.
reading.question: How does Filipp Filippovich react to the sudden crash and scream from elsewhere in the apartment?
options: He cries out and rushes toward the door
He tells Zina to handle it alone
reading.correct: He cries out and rushes toward the door
reading.explain: Startled by the noise, Filipp Filippovich shouts 'My God, something else!' and rushes toward the doors.

reading.ru: Затем высокое стекло, выходящее под самым потолком ванной в кухню, треснуло червивой трещиной и Из него вывалились два осколка, а за ними выпал громаднейших размеров кот в тигровых кольцах и с голубым бантом на шее, похожий на городового.
reading.question: What bursts through the high window between the bathroom and kitchen?
options: An enormous striped cat with a blue bow around its neck
reading.correct: An enormous striped cat with a blue bow around its neck
reading.explain: The high window cracks and shatters, and an enormous tiger-striped cat with a blue bow, looking like a policeman, tumbles through into the kitchen.

reading.ru: «Что вам надо?» «Говорящую собачку любопытно поглядеть», — ответила старуха заискивающе и перекрестилась.
reading.question: Why has the old woman come into the kitchen?
options: She is curious to see the talking little dog
She is looking for her lost cat
She works for the house committee
reading.correct: She is curious to see the talking little dog
reading.explain: The old woman explains, ingratiatingly, that she came out of curiosity to see the talking dog, crossing herself as she says it.

reading.ru: В разбитое окно под потолком показалась и высунулась в кухню физиономия полиграфа Полиграфовича.
reading.question: Whose face appears through the broken window into the kitchen?
reading.correct: Poligraf Poligrafovich's (Sharikov's)
reading.explain: Sharikov's face — twisted, scratched, and tearful — appears and pokes through the broken window into the kitchen.

reading.ru: А швейцар Федор с зажженной венчальной свечой Дарьи Петровны по деревянной лестнице лез в слуховое окно.
reading.question: How does the doorman Fyodor try to help resolve the bathroom crisis?
options: He climbs a wooden ladder toward the skylight, carrying Darya Petrovna's lit wedding candle
He breaks down the door with an axe
reading.correct: He climbs a wooden ladder toward the skylight, carrying Darya Petrovna's lit wedding candle
reading.explain: Fyodor the doorman climbs a wooden ladder toward the skylight, holding Darya Petrovna's lit wedding candle for light.

reading.ru: Зина и Дарья Петровна в подоткнутых до колен юбках с голыми ногами и Шариков с швейцаром, босые, с закатанными штанами, шваркали мокрыми тряпками по полу кухни и отжимали их в грязные ведра и раковину.
reading.question: What are the household members doing to deal with the flood in the kitchen?
options: Mopping the floor with wet rags, barefoot with skirts and trousers rolled up
Calmly waiting for professionals to arrive
Ignoring the water and continuing dinner
Arguing about whose fault it is instead of cleaning
reading.correct: Mopping the floor with wet rags, barefoot with skirts and trousers rolled up
reading.explain: Zina, Darya Petrovna, Sharikov, and the doorman all mop the kitchen floor with wet rags, barefoot, with skirts and trousers rolled up, wringing them into buckets and the sink.

reading.ru: — Знаете, Шариков, — переводя дух, отозвался Филипп Филиппович, — я положительно не видал более наглого существа, чем вы.
reading.question: What does Filipp Filippovich say to Sharikov after the chaos of the flood?
options: That he has never seen a more insolent creature than Sharikov
That he is impressed by Sharikov's quick thinking
That he plans to reward Sharikov for his effort
reading.correct: That he has never seen a more insolent creature than Sharikov
reading.explain: Catching his breath, Filipp Filippovich tells Sharikov he has positively never seen a more insolent creature than him.

reading.ru: Филипп Филиппович извлек три блестящих полтинника и вручил Федору.
reading.question: How does Filipp Filippovich compensate Fyodor for his trouble and expenses?
options: He gives him three shiny fifty-kopeck coins
He gives him a new coat
He refuses to pay him anything
reading.correct: He gives him three shiny fifty-kopeck coins
reading.explain: Filipp Filippovich takes out three shiny fifty-kopeck coins and hands them to Fyodor as payment.

reading.ru: Помилуйте, вас жалко, Филипп Филиппович.
reading.question: How does the chapter end, in Fyodor's final remark to the professor?
options: Fyodor says he feels sorry for Filipp Filippovich
Fyodor demands more money before leaving
Fyodor quits his job on the spot
Fyodor threatens to report Sharikov to the police
reading.correct: Fyodor says he feels sorry for Filipp Filippovich
reading.explain: The chapter closes with Fyodor's sympathetic remark, 'Have mercy, I feel sorry for you, Filipp Filippovich.'

highlight.question: Which sentence describes how the lamp creates an evening atmosphere in the dining room?
sentences: В столовой было совершенно по-вечернему, благодаря лампе под шёлковым абажуром.
Свет из буфета падал перебитый пополам зеркальные стёкла были заклеены косым крестом от одной фасетки до другой.
Филипп Филиппович, склонившись над столом, погрузился в развёрнутый громадный лист газеты.
highlight.explain: This sentence states that the dining room is completely evening-like in atmosphere thanks to the lamp under the silk shade.

highlight.question: Which two sentences show Sharikov angrily defending himself regarding the operation?
sentences: Чисто как в трамвае.
Что вы мне жить не даёте?!
И насчёт «папаши» – это вы напрасно.
Разве я просил мне операцию делать?
– человек возмущённо лаял.
highlight.explain: These sentences contain his defiant statements that he never asked for the operation and his claim that others are wrong to blame him.

highlight.question: Which two sentences reveal Filipp's concerns about what Sharikov is telling people and his previous instructions?
sentences: – Ах, ты, господи, – уныло воскликнул Филипп Филиппович, – встречаются, спрашивают…
Воображаю, что вы им говорите.
Ведь я же вам запрещал шляться по лестницам.
highlight.explain: The first shows his worry about what Sharikov tells the neighbors, and the second reveals his earlier order to keep Sharikov away from the stairs.

highlight.question: Which sentence contains Shvonder's request for the professor to write an official certificate about Sharikov?
sentences: – Что же, – заговорил Швондер, – дело несложное.
Пишите удостоверение, гражданин профессор.
Что так, мол, и так, предъявитель сего действительно Шариков Полиграф Полиграфович, гм…
Зародившийся в вашей, мол, квартире.
highlight.explain: This sentence directly asks the citizen professor to write a certificate confirming that the presenter is indeed Sharikov Poligraf Poligrafovich.

highlight.question: Which two sentences show Filipp's desperate plan to remove Sharikov from the apartment?
sentences: – Вот что, э…
– внезапно перебил его Филипп Филиппович, очевидно терзаемый какой-то думой, – нет ли у вас в доме свободной комнаты?
Я согласен её купить.
highlight.explain: These sentences reveal Filipp suddenly asking Shvonder if there is a free room in his house that he is willing to buy as a solution to his problem.

highlight.question: Which two sentences demonstrate Filipp's exasperation and his confrontation with Darya Petrovna?
sentences: – Вон, я говорю!
– Повторил Филипп Филиппович и глаза его сделались круглыми, как у совы.
Он собственноручно трахнул чёрной дверью за старухой.
– Дарья Петровна, я же просил вас.
highlight.explain: The first shows his dramatic reaction and the forceful way he closed the door behind the old woman, and the second contains his reproach to her for not following his instructions.
